articles.title: Limiting six sources of pharmaceuticals might slash mixture toxicity risk in rivers
articles.summary: Nature Geoscience, Published online: 12 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s41561-026-02101-2 A machine-learning model leverages 1,017 toxicity assays in three species and 24 geospatial predictors to generate high-resolution maps of toxicity from pharmaceutical mixtures in rivers worldwide. Analyses reveal that targeted management of six key sources of pharmaceuticals might substantially reduce the river areas at risk.

articles.title: Independent interferometric observable confirms black hole shadow in M87*

articles.title: Global fossil fuel emissions set to fall in 2026, but total CO2 keeps rising
articles.summary: Global fossil fuel emissions are projected to fall in 2026 as renewable energy and electric vehicles gain ground, but rising emissions from deforestation threaten to push total CO2 emissions to a new record. Scientists warn that the world's remaining carbon budget for limiting warming to 1.5°C could be exhausted in less than four years, even as a lasting decline in emissions appears increasingly within reach.

articles.title: Ocean absorbs more fossil fuel carbon while land uptake stalls, 30 years of data show
articles.summary: The ocean has been absorbing carbon dioxide from fossil fuel emissions at an increasing rate since 1990, while the net uptake of carbon by forests, soils and other land ecosystems has not grown, according to a new study led by scientists at UC San Diego's Scripps Institution of Oceanography.

articles.title: Oʻahu infrastructure threatened by tipping point in sea-level rise impacts

Earth’s early history told by 3.9-billion-year-old rocks from northern China
articles.summary: Nature, Published online: 11 November 2026; doi:10.1038/d41586-026-03499-w Ancient rocks in northern China reveal that by 3.95 billion years ago, surface-altered oceanic crust had been buried rapidly to depths greater than 50 kilometres and partly melted. This crust was derived from a mantle reservoir that had been left behind when the crust separated from the early mantle as early as 4.3 billion years ago.

articles.title: Hadean mantle depletion and 3.95-Gyr subduction implied by North China rocks

articles.title: Superheated magma could fuel towering lava fountains
articles.summary: Why do some volcanoes erupt with spectacular lava fountains while others release lava more quietly? Scientists have discovered that a hidden effect of extreme heat inside magma may help explain the difference. Experiments revealed that superheated magma can delay crystal formation for more than eight hours, compared with just 20 minutes in magma that has not been superheated.

Powered by supermassive black holes, these extraordinary cosmic beacons reveal a time when the first galaxies were still taking shape.

articles.title: A dead star is flashing radio waves every 8 minutes, and its partner looks a lot like the sun
articles.summary: Since 2022, astronomers have been puzzling over a new kind of cosmic object called long-period radio transients. These are objects that emit bright flashes of radio waves into space every few minutes to every few hours. Some have been traced back to binary systems consisting of a small, dim, cool star called a red dwarf in orbit with a stellar remnant called a white dwarf.

articles.title: A giant icy world hiding beyond Pluto could be our sixth dwarf planet
